members.title: Govt to rebuild Bangladesh as fascism-free dignified state: PM
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today, Saturday, said his government is committed to rebuilding a fascism-free Bangladesh as a dignified and exemplary state on the world stage, pledging continued respect and support for freedom fighters and their families. "The government's pledge is to place the independent Bangladesh, which the valiant freedom fighters courageously established for us, in a position of dignity," he said, adding that the state would continue to extend respect and support to the freedom fighters and their families to the best of its capacity and resources. . The Prime Minister was addressing a reception for gallantry award-winning freedom fighters of the Armed Forces and their heirs on the occasion of Armed Forces Day-2026. The reception was held this morning at the Army Multipurpose Complex in Dhaka Cantonment. Noting that freedom fighters were conferred gallantry titles such as Bir Sreshtha, Bir Uttam, Bir Bikram and Bir Protik for their heroic role in the Liberation War, the Prime Minister said more important than any title is the glory of fighting for and winning a nation's independence. "Not everyone gets the opportunity to achieve such glory in a lifetime. That is why the freedom fighters are unique and extraordinary," he said. . Addressing the freedom fighters and family members present, he said some of them had the good fortune to take part directly in the Liberation War, while others lost family members as martyrs. "All of you share that glory, directly or indirectly. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to you," he said. Recalling the sacrifices of 1971, the Prime Minister said independent Bangladesh was established at the cost of the lives of millions, the honour of countless mothers and sisters, and the sacrifices of those who were wounded and crippled. members.title: Constitution to be amended if necessary to permanently ban Awami League
members.lead: The State Minister for Local Government, Mir Shahe Alam, has stated that if necessary, the government and the opposition will amend the constitution through consensus to permanently ban the activities of the Awami League. He made this statement to journalists after the inauguration of Shaheed Abu Sayed Stadium in Rangpur on Saturday afternoon. The state minister said the defeated and banned organisation had thought that it could create anarchy by carrying out a few petrol bomb attacks and setting fire to a few police stations in different parts of Bangladesh, and then start something anew at the expense of the country's independence and sovereignty and the memory of martyrs such as Abu Sayed. These actions will bring no benefit. . Describing the current government as humane, patient, and trusting in democracy, Mir Shahe Alam said, ''From a humanitarian perspective, unlike the previous government, we do not want to eradicate them through disappearances, killings, or shootings. For this reason, we have handled everything with patience. If the people of a district think there is no need for a police station there, the government will not keep a police station there. If the people of a district believe that government offices, courts, and development are not needed in that district, the current government will not provide them. It will depend on what the people want. It has been proven to the people of Bangladesh that the activities-banned Awami League is a terrorist political party.'' . The State Minister said that it has been proven to the nation that the past interim government was correct and justified in banning them (Awami League). He said, ''The time has come to think anew—if the constitution is being amended, then to permanently ban the Awami League in Bangladesh anew, if necessary. . . the current government and opposition will do so through consensus by amending the constitution, Inshallah.''

members.title: Awami League’s dream of staging another 1/11 will turn into a nightmare: Hefazat-e-Islam
members.lead: Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has said that the activities-banned Awami League’s dream of staging another 1/11 will be turned into a nightmare. In a statement sent to the media today, Saturday, the party said the country’s sovereignty would remain unprotected unless Awami fascism was eradicated. It also said the Awami League must be banned as a political party through judicial proceedings at the tribunal for its responsibility for mass killings. In the statement, Hefazat-e-Islam Ameer Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Allama Sajedur Rahman said, “We will turn their (the Awami League’s) dream of staging another 1/11 into a nightmare.” .BNP clashes with activities-banned Awami League in Pabna. The statement added, “We do not believe that the media outlets seen working in favour of their anti-Bangladesh agenda will be spared when another mass resistance takes place.” The statement said the Awami League was no longer a political party. It said that, after carrying out mass killings in the face of the July mass uprising, the party’s leaders and activists had fled to India, proving themselves to be agents of hegemonic interests. With support from Delhi, the defeated forces of 2024 were once again attempting to destabilise Bangladesh through acts of arson and violence across the country under Awami fascism, it added. .Why the government is not cracking down on Awami League sabotage yet, and its strategy. The top Hefazat leaders said in the statement that the victims killed and injured in the Pilkhana, Shapla, July and anti-Modi movements were still waiting for justice. Public anger was growing towards those who spoke in favour of the Awami League and hegemonic interests on various talk shows and platforms without taking the victims’ demand for justice into consideration, they said. members.title: If united, no one will dare turn Bangladesh into a subservient state: PM
members.lead: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has said no one would ever again dare to turn Bangladesh into a subservient state if patriotic people, a democratic government accountable to the people and the armed forces remained united in the spirit of "Bangladesh First". “Deep conspiracies were hatched in the past to trample Bangladesh's independence and sovereignty and tarnish the image of the armed forces. But the armed forces have always played an important role in safeguarding the country's independence and protecting the interests of its people,” he said. The Prime Minister made the remarks this afternoon while addressing a reception at Senakunja in Dhaka Cantonment marking Armed Forces Day 2026. On arrival at the venue, Army Chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Navy Chief Admiral Khondkar Misbah Ul Azim and Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan received the Prime Minister and his wife Zubaida Rahman. The Prime Minister was then escorted to the stage, where the national anthem was played. . The Prime Minister said the armed forces played a landmark role in favour of the country and its people at every important juncture- the Liberation War of 1971, the soldiers-and-people's revolution of 7 November, 1975, and the anti-fascist mass uprising of 5 August, 2024. The premier said that just as brave freedom fighters had won independence by laying down their lives in 1971, brave students and people protected the freedom of the country and its people through the bloody mass uprising in 2024. He said there were two main responsibilities to honour the martyrs. First- to safeguard at any cost the independence and sovereignty won through their sacrifices, and second- to build the safe, self-reliant, democratic welfare state they had dreamt of. Highlighting the glorious history of the armed forces, the Prime Minister said their journey began with independence and the Liberation War.
